question: What can the public MSU GenSan thesis record establish about freshwater fish research in Tubajon, Dinagat Islands, and what is unavailable without the thesis text?

source.title: Freshwater Fish and Macroinvertebrate Assemblages of Zamboecozone, Barangay Talisayan, Zamboanga City and Tubajon, Dinagat Islands
source.recordMetadata: The repository record lists SY 2012 and a Bachelor of Science in Biology program.
source.access: The official MSU General Santos City thesis repository record and abstract were retrieved on 2026-10-31. The public record exposes no full-text PDF or attachment link. The repository describes document access as a service for registered users, but no sign-in was attempted. No alternate copy, author contact, or access-control bypass was used.

licenseReview.result: No item-specific copyright or reuse license is displayed on the public record page.
licenseReview.decision: Do not infer app publication permission from the public abstract. Retain only concise factual screening notes; no thesis text, species table, image, or map is reproduced.

studyContext.asReportedMethod: Kick-net and D-frame dip-net sampling of surface-water fish and macroinvertebrates, according to the abstract.
studyContext.dateInterpretation: The date string is malformed and does not clearly resolve the Tubajon field dates or the date-to-site pairing. Preserve it verbatim; no corrected sampling date is asserted.
studyContext.fullTextAndMethods: No thesis PDF, species table, complete sampling station list, station map, voucher data, or detailed index calculation was available on the public item page.

tubajonFishClaim.scope: The abstract-level claim is for Tubajon overall; it does not say which of the two named catchments yielded this fish or provide the other seven fish names.

abstractFindings.indexBoundary: These are abstract-reported macroinvertebrate biotic-index labels. Without the thesis methods, site crosswalk, full metric context, physical/chemical sampling and current monitoring, they are not current water-quality determinations, drinking-water safety results, fish-consumption advice or fishing restrictions.

interpretation.safeSummary: The public university record identifies an undergraduate thesis that studied fish and macroinvertebrates in surface waters at Tubajon, Dinagat Islands, as well as a separate Zamboanga City site. Its abstract reports eight fish species in Tubajon and names Puntius binotatus as dominant at 48.83% relative abundance. It provides no complete fish list or fish-by-catchment allocation. The displayed sampling-date string is unresolved, and the full thesis was not publicly linked on the record page.
notSupported: A complete or current Tubajon/Dinagat Islands freshwater-fish checklist.
Assigning Puntius binotatus or the other seven unnamed fish taxa to Diaz-Mabini versus Navarro catchment.
Corrected field dates, exact sampling stations, coordinates, stream geometry or specimen/voucher identities.
Current water quality, drinking-water safety, fish safety, contamination, legal fishing rules or harvest restrictions from the abstract's biotic-index labels.
Natural diet, bait suitability, abundance beyond the abstract's reported 2011-era relative-abundance summary, or present-day catchability.

disposition.reason: The institutional record exposes only an abstract, not the species table, detailed station allocation, full methods or item-specific reuse terms. Its sampling-date string is malformed, and the abstract's water-quality labels cannot support current safety or fishing guidance.

nextAction: Keep the Tubajon result as a research lead only. Continue searching for another directly accessible Caraga freshwater survey or specimen source; revisit this thesis only if its full text becomes available through the repository's ordinary authorized access process.

references.supports: Official repository title, author, SY 2012/program metadata, methods/date string and all abstract-level fish, macroinvertebrate and catchment-index claims.
The repository describes its document browse/view/download function and states that it is designed for university members; this does not grant item-level reuse rights.
